title.narrative: Blue Benguela Current: an integrated conservation and sustainable use of the Benguela Current Large Maritime Ecosystem (BCLME) for a sustainable blue economy

description.narrative:
The Multi-Donor Action ¿Blue Benguela Current¿ is jointly co-financed by the European Union and the German Federal Ministryfor Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by GIZ as part of the BMZ Global Programme ¿Sustainable Aquatic Food¿ (GP SAF). The duration of this Action is scheduled from 15.06.2024 to 31.03.2028 (45.5 months) with a total budget of 12,000,000 EUR (EU contribution 11,000,000 EUR and BMZ contribution 1,000,000 EUR). BMZ¿s total funding for the Global Programme ¿Sustainable Aquatic Food¿ is 17,000,000 EUR.

The Action is part of the EU¿s Multi-Annual Indicative Programme 2021-2027 for Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), which prioritises ¿Waters and Oceans¿ under its Green Transition priority area with the aim of promoting more sustainable use and management of oceans, coastal zones, river basins, and lakes in the region. The present Action specifically targets the Benguela Current Large Marine Ecosystem (BCLME) in a multi-level approach including activities at local, national and regional (BCC, SADC) levels. Although the primary focus is on the Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZs) of Angola, Namibia, and South Africa, the Action will also incorporate elements of the International Agreement on Marine Biodiversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ), adopted in June 2023.

The Overall Objective of the Action is to contribute to an inclusive and sustainable Blue Economy in the BCLME based on integrated conservation and sustainable use of the region¿s marine and coastal biodiversity and the associated ecosystem goods and services for the benefit of diverse social groups.

The Specific Objectives (Outcomes) of this Action are (1) to enhance the national and regional governance and integrated management of the Benguela Current Large Marine Ecosystem's marine biodiversity and natural resources supporting sustainable livelihoods, and (2) to leverage financial resources for the sustainable management of key marine biodiversity areas.

The Action has the following outputs:

1. Strengthened institutional capacities of the BCC (comprising the BCC secretariat, the Commission and the respective national Ministries of fisheries, environment and other marine related sectors).

2. Strengthened SADC regional fisheries policy processes and institutional capacity.

3. Diversified income of local communities, particularly of vulnerable groups and women, through sustainable use of marine biodiversity and resources including sustainable fisheries.

4. Enhanced management of marine biodiversity areas and Marine Protected Areas for the conservation and sustainable use of marine resources supporting sustainable livelihoods and food security.

5. Improved legal and institutional capacity for the implementation of ecosystem-based Marine Spatial Planning (MSP).

6. Innovative financing solutions developed to support Marine Protected Areas and/or Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measures for the conservation and sustainable management of fish stocks and other marine biodiversity.
